task: Propón en 80–100 palabras un proyecto para tu barrio que ayude a los vecinos a compartir algo (objetos, conocimientos, tiempo). Explica cómo funcionaría usando could, would y if.
paragraphs: How many times have you used your drill? If you are like most people, the answer is "almost never". Yet millions of homes have one, along with ladders, tents, sewing machines and other objects that spend most of their lives in a cupboard.

A few years ago, a group of neighbours in a London suburb had an idea: what if people could borrow these things, just like books from a library? They collected donations, found a small room in a community centre and opened a "library of things".

It works like this. Members pay a small yearly fee, or nothing if they can't afford it. They can then borrow a drill for the weekend, a projector for a party or a tent for a camping trip. When they bring the item back, volunteers check that it works and clean it for the next person.

The project has grown quickly. Similar libraries now exist in dozens of towns in Europe and North America. Supporters say they save money, reduce waste and free up space in small homes. "Why buy a carpet cleaner you'll use twice a year?" asks Grace, one of the founders.

But the founders say the biggest surprise was social. Volunteers run free workshops where people learn to repair a bicycle or fix a broken lamp. Older members teach younger ones how to use tools, and people who live on the same street meet for the first time. "People come to borrow a ladder and stay for a cup of tea," Grace laughs.

Of course, there are problems. Some items come back broken, and finding volunteers is not always easy. Still, the idea is spreading, and many people now think twice before buying something they will hardly ever use.
